analysis.title: Our Longer-Term Investment themes in focus
key_insights: UBS CIO's Longer-Term Investment (LTI) model ranks five themes as the most attractive entry points: Automation and robotics, Diversity and Equality, Aging in comfort, Energy transition(s), and Energy efficiency.

Shorter-term investors are advised to review exposure to Genetic therapies and Healthtech and consider one of the top five themes. The long-term outlook for both is unchanged, but they rank 13th or lower among 23 themes in the model over six to 12 months.
The ranking does not change conviction in the other LTI themes. UBS recommends diversifying across multiple themes to limit drawdown risk.

Identifying the next frontier is the only theme with significant Middle East exposure. Emerging and frontier markets fell after military conflict broke out in the Middle East and energy prices rose sharply, then resumed their rise on a solid global growth outlook. Near-term risk remains from geopolitics and disrupted Middle East energy flows.

UBS stays constructive on emerging and frontier markets over the medium term and prefers a broad, geographically diversified basket. Supports cited: concern over concentrated USD holdings, loose fiscal policy in major economies, and a screen for markets that convert GDP growth into earnings growth.

Automation and robotics stays at the top of the ranking on strong momentum and a favorable quality score. US ISM Manufacturing rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5 in September and beat expectations. The European manufacturing PMI was 52.7 in October, against a September multi-year high of 52.9 and a preliminary estimate of 52.4.

Automation and robotics drivers include industrial software and AI, humanoids addressing labor shortages, lagging robotics adoption in emerging markets, aging populations, and reshoring prompted by US tariffs.

Diversity and Equality stays in the top five on favorable valuation and quality score. The theme is diversified across sectors with a mix of defensive, value and growth. Legal challenges to affirmative action and diversity focus in some US states are a short-term risk.
Aging in comfort stays in the top five on attractive valuation. The theme leans toward financials, with health care sub-themes giving some downside protection in a volatile market.

Energy transition(s) entered the top five this month on strong momentum and a favorable quality score. Its energy and utilities exposure benefits from elevated oil prices, and the pickup in industrial activity adds a cyclical tailwind. BloombergNEF put 2023 energy transition investment at USD 1.77tr, up 17% y/y. UBS estimates cumulative energy and transition investment could exceed USD 100tr by 2050.

Energy efficiency stays in the top five on strong model momentum and quality. The Middle East crisis has put energy security back in focus, and oil is nearly 91% of final energy demand in transport. Global energy efficiency investment was about USD 800bn in 2025, and the IEA sees a need for an extra USD 1.3tr a year to meet climate targets.

Genetic therapies ranks low on valuation and quality, with weak momentum. Small and mid-sized biotech still face tight capital availability and limited visibility on commercialization and revenue growth. The unwinding of the biotech funding bubble that peaked in 2021 remains a challenge. UBS recommends switching to a top-ranked theme.

Healthtech ranks low on quality and momentum after a rally, especially in its tech segment. Tight financial conditions, slow adoption owing to reimbursement and regulatory hurdles, and trouble turning user growth into sustainable economics weigh on it. UBS sees AI potential in diagnostics, care delivery and cost management but no scalable data-driven growth drivers yet.
For health care exposure, UBS prefers its Longevity TRIO theme, made up mostly of large-cap, self-funding, cash-flow-generating companies that do not rely on capital markets.

The model ranks themes on valuation (mainly one-year trailing FCF yield), momentum (12-month price plus three-month earnings revisions) and quality (changes in profitability, financial health and efficiency). A qualitative overlay covers CIO House View consistency, risks and catalysts. Stock picking is excluded and the model is calibrated to minimize turnover.

Market-size estimates in the theme appendix include security and safety at USD 974bn in 2026 rising to USD 1,189bn by 2029 (about 7% a year), space economy at USD 1.3tr by 2040, and smart mobility rising from about USD 465bn to about USD 2tr by 2030.

sector_views.rationale: Improving manufacturing indicators (ISM Manufacturing 55.5, Europe PMI 52.7) and a cyclical recovery support the Automation and robotics and Energy efficiency themes.
The Energy transition(s) theme benefits from elevated oil prices and an industrial cyclical tailwind.
The Aging in comfort theme is geared toward financials, which UBS says have solid fundamentals and attractive valuations.
Constrained capital availability, limited commercialization visibility and weak model ranks on valuation, quality and momentum.
Low quality and momentum ranks after a rally, with slow adoption and no near-term growth drivers.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Beat expectations and sits well above 50, which points to ongoing expansion and supports the cyclical case for automation and energy efficiency.
Above 50 and above the preliminary estimate, which points to resilient European manufacturing momentum.

macro_indicators.indicator: Oil share of final energy demand in transport
macro_indicators.interpretation: Shows how exposed transport is to oil, which supports the energy efficiency case.

trade_ideas.description: Favor the top five LTI themes (Automation and robotics, Diversity and Equality, Aging in comfort, Energy transition(s), Energy efficiency) over Genetic therapies and Healthtech for a six to 12 month horizon.
trade_ideas.rationale: The top five rank highest in the quantitative model, and the two lagging themes have no identified near-term catalysts.
trade_ideas.risk: All investment decisions carry risks, including partial or total loss.

risk_factors: Near-term volatility in individual emerging and frontier markets from Middle East geopolitical risk and energy flow disruptions.
Legal challenges to affirmative action and diversity focus in some US states could hurt the Diversity and Equality theme in the short term.
Biotech funding constraints and the unwinding of the 2021 funding bubble weigh on Genetic therapies.
Tight financial conditions, reimbursement challenges and regulatory hurdles weigh on Healthtech.
Theme performance is sensitive to the economic cycle, so themes can outperform or underperform in different phases.
geopolitical: Military conflict in the Middle East caused a sharp rise in global energy prices and pressured emerging and frontier markets, which have since recovered.
Disruptions to energy flows from the Middle East remain a near-term risk for some equity markets in the Identifying the next frontier theme.
The Middle East crisis has put energy security back in focus for countries and corporations.
Recent US tariffs exposed global supply chain vulnerabilities and prompted companies to reshore production.

theme_stances.key_argument: The quantitative model ranks Automation and robotics, Diversity and Equality, Aging in comfort, Energy transition(s) and Energy efficiency as the most attractive entry points.
theme_stances.evidence: these themes currently offer the most attractive entry points

theme_stances.key_argument: Both rank low in the model and lack near-term positive catalysts, so shorter-term investors should consider a top-ranked theme.
theme_stances.evidence: our analysts do not identify any positive short-term catalysts

theme_stances.key_argument: Emerging and frontier economies are attractive over the medium term despite near-term Middle East risk, and a broad diversified basket is preferred.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to view emerging and frontier economies as attractive investment opportunities over the medium term
